bullets.body: FMRB executive order interagency draft circulated Wednesday hits a coordinated Friday pushback. AI Policy Institute, R Street, Public Knowledge, and Lawyers for Civil Justice file a joint open letter to OSTP and the White House Counsel's office arguing that any frontier-model pre-release notification regime relying on Defense Production Act §708 voluntary information-sharing authority — without an Administrative Procedure Act notice-and-comment window — is vulnerable to challenge under State Farm arbitrary-and-capricious review the moment a denied or delayed deployment lands in the DC Circuit. Senator Mark Warner (Senate Intel) and Senator Todd Young (Commerce) jointly request a classified briefing from NIST and the ODNI cyber lead on the Frontier Model Review Board threshold methodology before any final EO signs, with the briefing tentatively scheduled for May 15. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind publish brief statements supporting a comment window in principle while declining to oppose the §708 vehicle, holding the cohort consensus the May 7 reciprocity protocol relied on.

bullets.body: The trans-Atlantic counter-shape lands within 24 hours of the May 7 EU-UK joint memorandum. Singapore IMDA and Japan AISI publish a parallel reciprocity memorandum-of-cooperation accepting AISI-administered TLO-range cyber-evaluation runs as satisfying their respective frontier-model voluntary-disclosure regimes, with a 120-day placement window. Canada CCCS and Australia ASD ACSC sign on as observers and pre-commit to mirror language by Q3 2026. The Singapore/Japan MoC explicitly cites the May 7 EU-UK protocol as its template and the Mythos and GPT-5.5 results as the operational threshold. A four-jurisdiction recognition perimeter is now visible inside one news cycle, putting US absence from the cyber-eval reciprocity layer in sharper relief as the FMRB EO continues drafting.

bullets.body: UK NCSC's CNI advisory expansion converts to action. NHS Digital, DWP, and HMRC each publish revised May 15 maintainer-facing repository-lockdown lists, with HMRC alone wall-walling 327 internal repositories and DWP's count at 196. HM Treasury extends the public-sector LLM-coding-assistant procurement pause from one week to a 30-day formal review and adds Google Gemini Code Assist plus Microsoft GitHub Copilot for Government tenants to a temporarily-suspended-vendors annex pending Mythos-class capability disclosure under the AI Procurement Common Standard. Cabinet Office requests a written submission from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft by May 22 on offensive-cyber-capability test results conducted against UK-public-sector source-code estates. The first sovereign procurement freeze with named-vendor scope hits.

bullets.body: Cerebras Systems opens for trading on Nasdaq under ticker CBRS at $151.40, +18.3% over the $128 IPO price, briefly touching $158.20 intraday before settling near $148 at close on volume of ~28M shares. Fully-diluted market cap closes near $31.4B, putting Cerebras above the original $26.6B target by ~18% on day one. OpenAI's $1B warrant package now marks at roughly $4.9B paper gain at the close-of-day reference. Lock-up expires October 2026 (180 days). Buyside notes from Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Citi initiate Buy ratings with $165-$185 12-month price targets that explicitly cite the Apr 2026 OpenAI 1GW first-data-center commitment plus the still-undisclosed Saudi Aramco Digital MoU as upside drivers. The first-day pop becomes the operative reference for the SambaNova, Groq, and Tenstorrent S-1 cohort behind it.

Sell-side analyst desks lift their AI-services 10-Q footnote breakout probability for the Q1 2027 fiscal-cycle landing toward the high end of the prediction range. bullets.body: Nvidia and AMD pre-announce supply-allocation guidance ahead of the Q2 print cycle. Nvidia files an 8-K disclosing that Vera Rubin sampling has reached production-volume customer commitments for nine of the top ten hyperscaler and neocloud accounts, with H1 2027 NVL576 rack revenue now backlog-covered through Q3 2027 at current Blackwell B200 production cadence (~1,000 NVL72 racks/week). AMD CFO supplements the May 5 print with a separate 8-K confirming a 6.2GW total Helios + MI450 H2 2026 commitment book across Microsoft Azure, Oracle, OpenAI (the standing 1GW first data center already disclosed), Crusoe, CoreWeave, Lambda, plus a previously-undisclosed 0.8GW Tencent Cloud commitment for Asia-Pacific deployment, lifting AMD's data-center forward visibility to the top of analyst Q3 estimates. The dual 8-Ks crystallize the AI-accelerator duopoly forward-cadence record now on file.

bullets.body: Shadowserver and Censys publish day-eight scans on n8n CVE-2026-21858 (Ni8mare). Internet-exposed pre-1.121.0 instances drop from ~14,200 to ~8,300 (-41.5% in 24 hours) following the CISA KEV-catalog addition, with the steepest drops in Germany (1,920 to 980) and France (880 to 410). Roughly 47% of remaining exposed instances are still unpatched. Censys honeypot telemetry observes a 4.8x spike in exploitation attempts on the n8n REST webhook entry point during the first 12 hours after KEV listing, consistent with opportunistic scanning by commodity-tier exploit kits now incorporating the Ni8mare PoC. NHS England issues a separate emergency advisory naming Ni8mare among an enumerated list of agentic-AI workflow-platform CVEs that block migration into the NHS Federated Data Platform technology estate.

bullets.body: Two new agentic-AI tooling-stack CVEs land 24 hours after the LangGraph + LiteLLM disclosure pair. CrewAI CVE-2026-44352 (CVSS 8.7) is a deserialization vulnerability in the agent-task-checkpoint loader allowing arbitrary code execution by a malicious checkpoint file uploaded via a connected RAG storage. Haystack CVE-2026-44391 (CVSS 9.4) is an unauthenticated path-traversal in the deepset-cloud agent-tool registry permitting attacker-controlled file reads on the registry host plus pivot to AWS instance-metadata endpoints. CrewAI patches in v0.118.2 same-day; Haystack v2.21.4 ships the fix. Both CVEs are added to the OWASP GenAI Exploit feed within hours; Aikido and Sysdig joint write-up estimates the broader open-source agentic-orchestrator codebase contains a structurally similar exposure pattern across at least seven additional unmaintained agent-checkpoint loaders. Multi-vendor weekly disclosure cadence is now confirmed.

bullets.body: MCP-server attack-surface telemetry posts a third weekly update. Joint Adversa AI / Wiz / Sysdig data places exposed servers at ~10,400 (up from ~9,400 a week prior, +10.6%) with growth slowing as Microsoft Defender for Cloud's MCP-server threat-detection module GA from May 7 takes effect: 19% of net-new MCP servers seen on Defender-protected estates were quarantined within their first 30 minutes versus the unprotected baseline. Cisco Astrix Security (closed May 4 acquisition) ships a co-branded MCP-server identity gateway that integrates with the Defender XDR feed plus Microsoft Agent 365 audit ledger. The combined telemetry layer lands as the first cross-vendor agentic-AI control-plane tooling stack with data-plane visibility on >60% of new MCP-server provisioning events.

Claude Code 3.0 sandboxed-skill registry sees 11,400 skills published and 612K skill installs within the first 24 hours, with 87% of skills installed via the per-tenant capability-gating workflow rather than ad-hoc copy-paste. Per-tenant Mythos Preview gating is enabled by 38 enterprise customers including JPMorgan Chase, Booz Allen Hamilton, Mandiant Consulting, and Raytheon, all under the new contractual ethics-and-misuse rider. Simon Willison's annotation cites the registry's signed-version pinning as the structural answer to the agent-skills attack-surface concern raised earlier in April. Anthropic confirms Project Glasswing telemetry feeds into the registry's quarantine-evidence dashboard, with 14 Mythos-class skills auto-quarantined day-one for failing the per-tenant capability gate.

bullets.body: Unsloth ships a Hugging Face joint paper plus three follow-on fine-tuning recipes. The arxiv preprint Router-Only LoRA for Mixture-of-Experts Models presents the formal evaluation behind the May 7 Qwen3.6-Max router-only training mode, reporting ablation across Qwen3.6-Max, Mixtral 8x22B, DBRX, and Kimi K2.6. Router-only LoRA recovers 71-78% of full-LoRA-on-experts accuracy across the four models at 8-13% of training-step time and 11-16% of peak VRAM. New recipes ship for Llama 4 Behemoth-class router-only tuning (target H100 + B200 single-node), Kimi K2.6 router-only on RTX 6000 Ada workstation tier (96GB VRAM), and Mixtral 8x22B router-only adaptation for sovereign-cloud customers requiring no Hugging Face dependency at inference time. The router-only mode pairs with Unsloth's standing 12x faster MoE training, ultra-long-context Reinforcement Learning, and 7x longer context support.

bullets.body: vLLM v0.11.1 plus SGLang RadixArk v0.5.4 land Friday with security and performance follow-ups. vLLM v0.11.1 patches a CVSS 7.4 prefix-cache poisoning issue tracked as CVE-2026-44512 (cross-tenant prefix-cache key collision under multi-tenant deployment) and adds a new disaggregated-prefill mode mirroring Cloudflare Infire's edge architecture. SGLang RadixArk v0.5.4 ships a 2.1x speedup on tool-calling-heavy agentic workloads via RadixAttention-aware tool-result-cache reuse plus a CVSS 8.1 fix for an authenticated server-side template injection (CVE-2026-44567) discovered by Trail of Bits during the post-Cerebras IPO inference-stack red-team sweep. The Yotta Labs benchmark refresh now places vLLM at ~14,650 tok/s on the canonical shared-prefix workload (vs ~14,200 a day prior) and SGLang RadixArk at ~17,300 tok/s (vs ~16,200), narrowing the gap to 15.3% at the H100 tier.

Cerebras unveils the next-generation CS-4 wafer-scale engine with 1.2x the on-wafer SRAM, an upgraded 6.4Tb/s SwarmX fabric for cross-system clustering, and a published peak training throughput of 71 PFLOPS dense BF16 versus CS-3's 56 PFLOPS, with first customer engineering-sample shipments targeted for Q1 2027. OpenAI confirms its standing $10B multi-year supply agreement covers CS-4 deliveries inside the second-data-center commitment announced earlier in the year. Cerebras CTO comments that CS-4 specifically targets Mixture-of-Experts router-only training plus ultra-long-context RL workloads, citing the Unsloth + Hugging Face joint preprint published the same morning. Pairs with the Nvidia Vera Rubin and AMD Helios H2-2026 cadence to crystallize the three-vendor AI-accelerator roadmap.

bullets.body: Tenstorrent ships its first Wormhole Galaxy production rack. Tenstorrent announces general availability of its Galaxy rack, configured with 32 Wormhole-derived Quasar n300 boards (8,192 RISC-V Tensix cores plus 16 ARM A-class management cores) targeting inference-throughput-optimized open-architecture workloads. First customers are CoreWeave, Lambda Labs, and Crusoe, with Hyundai's Robotics Metaplant Application Center adopting Galaxy for on-prem humanoid policy fine-tuning and inference. Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller confirms the IPO bridge round at $3.4B previously reported with Hyundai and Samsung Foundry as co-anchors closed Wednesday, with a confidential S-1 submission targeted for July. The third independent AI-accelerator vendor with shipping production hardware in 2026 lands.

bullets.body: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Robotics expand the commercial Atlas roster. Hyundai's Robotics Metaplant Application Center confirms a 60-unit Atlas commercial deployment at Hyundai Steel's Dangjin Works for hot-rolled-coil handling and a 24-unit deployment at Kia's Slovak Zilina plant for paint-line subassembly. The Atlas commercial roster now spans automotive (Hyundai, Kia), heavy-industry (Hyundai Steel), and battery manufacturing (LG Energy Solution) inside a single quarter, with Boston Dynamics reporting the average per-unit MTBF improvement at 2.6x across pilot-to-production transitions. bullets.body: The arxiv RL-reasoning plus agentic-coordination wave continues with three new preprints. Self-Generated Process Critiques at Scale (arxiv 2605.05702) extends the May 6 verifier-free process-reward paradigm with a scaled study on 13B + 70B base models reporting 6.4-9.1% absolute gain on math-reasoning benchmarks while removing all human-annotated process-reward labels. Cooperative Search Trees with Role-Asymmetric Agents (arxiv 2605.05789) provides the proof-of-correctness companion to the May 6 multi-agent MCTS paper, formalizing convergence guarantees under role-asymmetric reward structures. Adaptive Inference Compute Routing for Mixture of Specialists Across Trust Boundaries (arxiv 2605.05821) extends the May 6 inference-routing paper with a security-aware variant that respects per-tenant capability-gating boundaries (the Project Glasswing primitive), reporting 41% inference-cost reduction with formal guarantees on no-cross-tenant-information-leakage.

bullets.body: DeepMind publishes a long-context RL stability paper directly relevant to the Unsloth router-only training mode. Stable Long-Context Reinforcement Learning via Router-Aware Advantage Decomposition (arxiv 2605.05844) shows that decomposing the policy-gradient advantage along Mixture-of-Experts router-decision boundaries materially improves training stability for long-context Reinforcement Learning runs, recovering full-LoRA-on-experts effective gradient signal in router-only training mode for context lengths beyond 128K tokens. The paper explicitly cites the Unsloth + Hugging Face router-only LoRA evaluation as the base setup and reports the technique closing the long-context training-stability gap that previously prevented router-only mode from being used for ultra-long-context Reinforcement Learning. The paper lands the same day as the Unsloth recipes for Llama 4 Behemoth, Kimi K2.6, and Mixtral 8x22B router-only training.
